Order 
This Miscellaneous Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed at the instance of the appellant-Insurance Company challenging the award dated 25.10.2005 passed by the First Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Guna (M.P.) in Claim Case No.
54/2003, whereby compensation of Rs.1,75,000/- was awarded in favour of the claimants.
2.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Guna (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The date of accident as well as the finding of negligence recorded by the Claims Tribunal are not in dispute and have attained finality.
The controversy involved in the present appeal is confined only to the question of liability of the Insurance Company.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company contended that the impugned award is illegal and contrary to the evidence on record insofar as it fastens liability upon the Insurance Company.

It is submitted that the offending tractor was insured only for agricultural purposes,
whereas at the time of the accident it was admittedly being used for carrying passengers of a marriage party NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4709 2 MA-1298-2005 (Barat).
Such use of the vehicle constituted a clear violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The Claims Tribunal itself recorded a categorical finding regarding breach of policy conditions, yet erroneously held the Insurance Company liable.
In absence of any contract of insurance covering such use of the vehicle, the appellant could not have been made liable to indemnify the award.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 Hence, prayed for setting aside the impugned award and sought exoneration from liability.

4. Heard learned counsel for the Insurance Company and perused the entire record.
5.

On perusal of paragraph 21 of the impugned award, it is evident that the Claims Tribunal recorded a specific finding that the offending tractor was being used for carrying passengers of a marriage party and that such use amounted to violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
From perusal of Insurance Policy (Ex. D-8), it is also clear that no premium was paid for carrying any passenger or gratuitous passenger on the tractor or trolley.
Therefore, the use of the vehicle at the time of the accident was wholly unauthorized and in breach of the policy conditions.

6. In National Insurance Company Limited vs. Bakaridan & Others , 2017 ACJ 2524, it was held that if a passenger travelling on the mudguard of a tractor dies in an accident caused by rash and negligent driving, the Insurance Company cannot be saddled with liability, as the seating capacity of a tractor is only one person, i.e., the driver.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Bakaridan & Others , 2017 ACJ 2524
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since no premium is paid for carrying passengers on the tractor or trolley, the owner alone would be liable for payment of compensation.

7. In New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs. Asha Rani , AIR 2003 SC 607, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that passengers are not permitted to travel on a tractor, and consequently, the Insurance Company cannot be held liable.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs. Asha Rani , AIR 2003 SC 607
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4709 3 MA-1298-2005 claimants are entitled to recover compensation only from the owner and driver of the tractor, who shall be jointly and severally liable to pay the same.

8. In view of the settled position of law and the categorical findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal regarding violation of the policy conditions, this Court is of the considered opinion that the fastening of liability upon the Insurance Company is unsustainable in law.
Accordingly, the findings of the Claims Tribunal to that extent are modified.
The appellant-Insurance Company is exonerated from liability to pay the compensation amount.
The claimants shall be entitled to recover the awarded compensation amount from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle, who shall be jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award.
9. If the Insurance Company has already deposited any amount in pursuance of the impugned award, it shall be entitled to withdraw the same, in accordance with law.
10. Accordingly, the Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed in the aforesaid terms and stands disposed of.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
